note: Altra, ethanol and biodiesel producer, Los Angeles (the firm's 2008 listing). Its state after the 2008-09 ethanol collapse and the firm's round were not established.

Biogen (BIIB), Cambridge MA; market cap $33.37B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis). The prefilled acquired and DK are a wrong join: the firm's own exit field reads IPO / BIIB. Biogen itself listed in 1983, so the firm's 1986 entry was IDEC Pharmaceuticals (founded 1985), the legal survivor of the 2003 merger that became Biogen; the base also carries 'idec-pharmaceuticals' (first seen 1986), one company carried twice. No round is on record.
Biosite, emergency-room diagnostics, San Diego (Brook Byers); bought by Inverness Medical in 2007. The firm's round is not on record.
BioSurface Technology, Cambridge MA; merged into Genzyme in 1994 (Genzyme Tissue Repair), acquired as the Greylock and Sutter Hill rows read. No round is on record.

Bit9, endpoint security (Ted Schlein). It merged with Carbon Black in 2014 and took its name; Carbon Black was bought by VMware in 2019. The Carbon Black S-1 (2018) shows KPCB XII funds holding 8.8% and buying a small slice of the Series F (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1366527/000104746918002643/a2235165zs-1.htm); the round the firm first entered is not named.

Blue Nile, online diamonds, Seattle; taken private by Bain and Bow Street in 2017. Its S-1 (2004) lists KPCB Holdings with 14.2% before the offering (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1091171/000089102004000321/v97093orsv1.htm), but the preferred series the funds bought is not stated in the pages read, so undetermined.

BorderX Lab (Beyond app), cross-border e-commerce into China, Sunnyvale and Shanghai. The firm's own post carries the release: '$20m in a Series B financing round led by Kleiner Perkins' (2018-05-08), with the firm first on the grid that year.
Boston Scientific, Marlborough MA. The firm dates its entry to 1991, the year before the 1992 IPO; no round is on record.

Broadwing Corporation is Corvis Corporation renamed in 2004 after Corvis bought Broadwing Communications; Level 3 bought it in 2007. The base also carries 'corvis-corp' (the 2001 13G filer), one company twice. No round is on record.

Built Technologies, construction-finance software, Nashville. The firm dates its entry to 2017 (Early, now Prior); no source names its round. Mark: the $125M Series D led by TCV at $1.5B (Pulse 2.0, 2021), stale, as the TCV row reads.

Bulletin, flexible retail and wholesale marketplace for independent brands, New York (YC W17). Kleiner Perkins joined the $2.2M seed with Flybridge, Afore and others (TechCrunch 2017-05-24). Status acquired as the YC row reads. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

The firm's Bump is the streetwear resale marketplace (sobump.com, YC W18, founded in the UK), later the sneaker community 'Secured' (the 2022 grid link), not Bump Technologies. Kleiner Perkins joined the $7.5M Series A led by e.ventures, announced 2019-04-10 as the company moved from New York to London (TechCrunch), but the firm listed it in December 2018, so the entry round is not settled. The a16z, Felicis, Sequoia and YC rows are Bump Technologies (acquired by Google 2013), a name collision; the base's 'secured' row is likely this company renamed.

Calixa, sales software for product-led companies (distributed team). Kleiner Perkins led the $12M Series A (TechCrunch 2021-11-09); TechCrunch's search shows no later round. The firm dropped it from the grid after 2023; its state and city were not established.

Callaway Digital Arts, children's apps (Sesame Street, Hasbro), an iFund position (Aileen Lee, before Cowboy Ventures); New York (low confidence). TechCrunch's search shows no round; state after 2013 not established.

Cameo, personalised celebrity videos, Chicago (Wikipedia); the Wikidata IT is a homonym. 'Cameo closed a $50 million Series B round led by Kleiner Perkins' (release, Chicago, 2019-06-25). The 2021 $1B figure later collapsed, so below_1b, aligned with the five sibling rows.

Captions (NOCAP Inc.), AI video creation, New York. The company's post: $25M Series B 'led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from existing investors Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, and SV Angel' (2023-06-22), so the firm entered there; the firm's own post of that day is titled for the Series B. The a16z row's 'a16z led the Series B (2022)' conflicts with this. Momentum check 2026-09-30 by web search: about $250M at the B and about $500M in 2024, no $1B+ round.
Cardiovascular Devices (CDI), cardiovascular monitoring, Irvine CA (low confidence); bought by 3M (the firm's exit field). The firm dates its entry to 1982; no round is on record.

Cartesia, real-time voice models, San Francisco. The December 2024 seed led by Index names no Kleiner Perkins (TechCrunch); the firm's post of 2025-03-11 says 'we're thrilled to partner with Cartesia and lead its Series A', so the entry is the Series A; the page's 2024 year is the close year. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (TechCrunch's search and its 2026 unicorn list): no $1B+ priced round, as the General Catalyst row found.
Castlight Health, San Francisco; bought by Vera Whole Health for about $370M in 2022 (Wikipedia). The firm dates its entry to 2010 (Early); no source names its round.
Celladon, gene therapy for heart failure, San Diego; merged with Eiger BioPharmaceuticals in 2016 (Celladon was the listed shell), acquired as prefilled. No round naming the firm is on record.
Cenergistic, energy-conservation programmes for schools and institutions, Dallas; last known operating (low confidence). No round naming the firm is on record.

Ceno Technology, messaging software for Chinese carriers and enterprises, Shanghai (the firm's China listing). A KPCB China position, provisional IN under X1; state after 2014 and the round not established.

Chainguard, secure open-source software supply chain, Kirkland WA. The firm's post (2025-04-23): 'We are thrilled to be partnering with Chainguard and leading their Series D', and its page dates the investment to 2025. Mark: $3.5B after the $356M Series D led by Kleiner Perkins and IVP (Built In Seattle, 2025-04-24), as the sibling rows read; an October 2025 growth investment came at the same mark (Lightspeed row). Momentum check 2026-09-30 (TechCrunch's search): nothing newer.

Chill (chill.com), social video discovery (Chi-Hua Chien, before Goodwater). Kleiner Perkins was in the $1.5M angel round with Redpoint and Atlas (TechCrunch 2011-09-06), a seed. State and city not established. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

China Auto Rental (zuche.com), Beijing. The firm's own 2012 page reads 'Acquired by Legend Holdings'; the business later listed in Hong Kong as CAR Inc. A KPCB China position (Tina Ju, not a TDF-era deal), provisional IN under X1; the fund's round is not named.

The 2010 China listing's stealth P2P personal-credit platform in Beijing matches CreditEase, which KPCB China backed that year; the base also carries 'credit-ease' (first seen 2012), very likely the same company, so this row should merge into it. Provisional IN under X1; status read as CreditEase's (operating, private).
A stealth credit-scoring and fraud-prevention company on KPCB China's 2010 listing, with no name, city or later page; the company cannot be identified, so stage, band and graduation are undetermined.

The 2010 China listing's stealth forestry company ('largest manufacturer of turpentine products in China', Hainan province); the 2012 pages carry the same description as 'Asia Forestry', so this row and 'asia-forestry' are one company. Provisional IN under X1; no city below the province.

ChineseAll, digital literature, Beijing, now COL Group (Shenzhen 300364). Market cap CNY 17.03B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis): CNY 17.03B @ ECB 2026-09-30 (CNY/EUR 7.613, EUR/USD 1.1355) = $2.54B. A KPCB China position (Tina Ju, not a TDF-era deal), provisional IN under X1; the fund's round is not named.

Chiral Quest, chiral catalysts for pharmaceutical manufacturing, Shanghai (the firm's China listing; James Huang, Wei Zhou). A KPCB China position, provisional IN under X1; state and round not established.

Chukou1, cross-border e-commerce logistics, Guangzhou (low confidence on the city); still on the firm's grid through 2024, read as operating. A KPCB China position (Tina Ju), provisional IN under X1; round not named.

Chutney Technologies, dynamic web-content caching, Atlanta (medium confidence), a Vinod Khosla deal from his KP years (before 2004). State and round not established. The YC row 'Chutney' (Bangalore) is a different company with the same name.

ClearStory Data, Menlo Park. Its first round (March 2012) named Google Ventures, a16z and Khosla, not Kleiner Perkins; the firm's page was captured in 2013 and KPCB is named in the $21M Series B of March 2014 (TechCrunch), so the entry is the $9M Series A of December 2012 (model, medium). Acquired by Alteryx in 2019.
Cleartrip, online travel, Mumbai; Kleiner Perkins, Ram Shriram and DAG Ventures were early investors (Wikipedia) but no round is dated. Acquired by Flipkart in April 2021.

Codecademy, New York. The October 2011 Series A names no Kleiner Perkins; the firm is named in the $10M second round of June 2012 (TechCrunch), which Wikipedia calls the Series B, so Growth. Acquired by Skillsoft for about $525M (announced December 2021).

Codeium, later Windsurf, AI coding (Mountain View). The firm's posts: 'We are thrilled to partner with them and lead their Series B' (2024-01-30), and Leigh Marie's first investment at the firm, the Series B closed in late 2023. Cognition acquired Windsurf in July 2025. The base also carries 'windsurf', the same company.
Codon Devices, synthetic biology, Cambridge MA; wound down in 2009. No round naming the firm is on record.

Cognition (Devin), San Francisco. The firm's page dates the investment to 2026 (Growth), but neither the Series D announcement (2026-05-27, $26B) nor the Series E report (TechCrunch 2026-09-08, $2B at $48B) names Kleiner Perkins, so the round is undetermined. The firm held Windsurf, which Cognition bought in July 2025; whether the Cognition stake is sale consideration for Windsurf is worth checking. Mark: $48B.
